title: Distinguishing Three-CNF Satisfiability
statement: Let a binary encoding of three-CNF formulas and an encoded maximization model be given. Suppose every canonical formula encoding is a valid instance, its optimum is at most $1$, and its optimum is $1$ exactly when the formula is satisfiable. If a polynomial-time algorithm returns a feasible solution on every valid instance and has value at least $1$ whenever the optimum is at least $1$, then any polynomial-time threshold test whose output is the one-bit indicator of whether the algorithm's value is at least $1$ distinguishes satisfiable from unsatisfiable formulas: it outputs true on every encoded satisfiable formula and false on every encoded unsatisfiable formula.
hypotheses_covered: A binary encoding of three-CNF formulas
Every canonical formula encoding is a valid maximization instance
The optimum of each encoded formula is at most $1$
The optimum is $1$ exactly when the formula is satisfiable
The algorithm is a polynomial-time map and returns a feasible solution on every valid instance
The algorithm returns value at least $1$ whenever the optimum is at least $1$
The threshold test is a polynomial-time map
The threshold test's output is exactly the one-bit indicator of whether the algorithm's value is at least $1$
replaced:
Let a binary encoding of exact-three-literal CNF formulas and an encoded maximization
model for those formulas be given. Suppose every encoded formula is a valid instance,
its optimum is at most $1$, and its optimum is $1$ exactly when the formula is
satisfiable. If a polynomial-time algorithm always returns a feasible solution on valid
instances and achieves value at least $1$ whenever the optimum is at least $1$, and a
polynomial-time test outputs the single bit indicating whether the algorithm's value is
at least $1$, then that test distinguishes satisfiable from unsatisfiable formulas on
the promise problem of valid formula encodings: it outputs true for satisfiable formulas
and false for unsatisfiable formulas.
